chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: The Cotton Club and Connie's Inn in Harlem
summary: He describes the Cotton Club bands and stars, shows staged by Leonard Reid and Clarence Robinson, a mostly white clientele, and Connie's Inn where he got Chuck a job.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Had you performed at the Cotton Club yet?
Oh, a long time before that.
Could we go back to that time when you first performed at the Cotton Club? What was the Cotton Club?
It was a night club where all the leads from downtown would come

up to this night club in Harlem, you know? They had Cab Calloway's Band, they had Fletcher Henderson, they had Duke Ellington, these are band leaders, you know. They had the Nicholas Brothers, The Berry Brothers. They had Nina Mae McKinney, George (inaudible) Washington, Orlando Robison, Hazel Scott, Peg Leg Bates, Ada Brown -- these are all entertainers now.
It was just basically --
Entertaining. That's all, entertaining, it's a club.
Who would stage the shows?
We had Leonard Reid. Had Clarence Robinson.
They were directing the shows?
Yeah, they'd stage the shows.
And basically each performer would come in and do their own --

Their own act, yeah. And they would set the girls up -- Leonard Reid and Clarence Robinson, they would get the chorus line and had a chorus line dance, and set that up and schedule the show, you know. And routine the show.
Was Bill Robinson there, too?
No, uh-uh.
Well, was it the type of club that was a well-known place in Harlem but it catered primarily to whites, is that correct?
Not primarily, they's the ones that patronized it, though. They had the money to spend to go there, man.
It cost --
Yeah.
Did the acts get paid well?
Oh, yeah, oh, yeah. They had the other club called Connie's
Inn, it was between 125th and 135th on 7th Avenue next to the Lafayette Theater, Corners Inn. That had a lot of entertainment, nice shows, too. I got Chuck a job in there.
Had Chuck and Chuckles come into the picture yet? At this point?
No. No, no. No they come in the part where we go -- we got to go -- I've got to go to England and come back now.
